The starting place of love, hopes, and dreams. Growing up in a small town, strong family values were instilled in my siblings and me. I was my dad's right-hand man from a young age.

Remodeling has become a strong passion of mine, and I take pride in transforming a pre-existing space and creating a new masterpiece.

THE BAYSHORE DIFFERENCE
What Makes a Bayshore
Remodel Feel Different.

The Bayshore Difference is not a slogan. It is a clear promise about how we prepare, protect, communicate, and stand behind the work in your home.

01
Clarity Before Disruption.

We define the layout, selections, key materials, and construction direction before your space is opened up, so you have fewer surprises and a clearer path forward.

02
Respect for Your Home.

Dust control, daily cleanup, and thoughtful protection are part of the process—not extras—so the rooms around the project remain cared for.

03
One Team That Owns the Details.

A dedicated project manager coordinates the work, communicates the next step, and walks the finished space with you before we call it complete.

SEE THE FULL BAYSHORE DIFFERENCE →
THE BAYSHORE STANDARD
Trust Has to Be
Built Into the Process.

A remodel is a big thing to hand over to someone. We earn that trust through a detailed plan, honest communication, a protected home, and a written commitment to the work after we leave.

01
Design Before Demolition

Selections, layout, and construction direction are understood before the first tool comes out.

02
Materials Before Demo

For applicable work, cabinetry and key materials are confirmed before your space is opened up.

03
One Accountable Team

A dedicated project manager coordinates the details and keeps communication clear.

OUR WRITTEN PROMISE
Warranty With
Specifics.

We put coverage in writing because “we stand behind our work” is not enough on its own.

2 YEARS
Painting Workmanship

Interior and exterior painting carries a two-year limited warranty for peeling, bubbling, or cracking caused by improper preparation or application.

30 DAYS
Touch-Up Visit

Within 30 days of completion, we return to address normal settling or minor scuffs discovered after you move back in.

1 YEAR
Remodeling Labor

All remodeling labor and workmanship is covered for one year from completion and final walkthrough. We also help clients understand manufacturer coverage on installed products.

READ OUR WARRANTY

THE BAYSHORE DIFFERENCE
The Standards Behind
Every Finished Space.

The difference is not a slogan. It is the planning, protection, communication, and craftsmanship we bring to every room—from the first conversation through the final walkthrough.

01
Plan Before We Open It Up.

For kitchens and baths, the layout, selections, and construction direction are understood before demolition begins, helping prevent avoidable surprises.

02
Protect What We Are Not Remodeling.

Dust control, daily cleanup, and a respectful jobsite are built into the work so the rest of your home stays cared for while your project moves forward.

03
One Vision Across Every Room.

For whole-home work, the kitchen, bathrooms, flooring, paint, built-ins, and transitions are coordinated as one finished environment—not a collection of disconnected decisions.

04
Recommend the Right Cabinet Solution.

We are direct about whether refacing, refinishing, or a larger remodel is the best fit for your cabinet boxes, layout, style, and investment range.

05
Stand Behind the Details.

We communicate clearly, complete a final walkthrough together, and back the work with written coverage and a practical touch-up visit after completion.

06
Specialists With 10+ Years Each.

Every trade on our team, from demolition and plumbing to electrical, tile, carpentry and paint, is a specialist with at least 10 years in that one trade. Together that is more than 50 years of specialized experience on every project, with Bayshore keeping the finish standard, communication and final result accountable.

07
Written Confidence After the Walkthrough.

We complete a final walkthrough together and stand behind our work with written workmanship coverage, so the commitment continues after your space is finished.

OUR APPROACH
The Kitchen Is Where Everyone Ends Up. It’s Worth Getting Right.

We design your kitchen before we touch it — detailed renderings you approve, so you know exactly what you’re getting. Your cabinetry arrives at your home before demolition day, which means your kitchen doesn’t sit torn apart waiting on a delivery truck. And one project manager runs the whole job, so you always know who to call.

Custom cabinetry, quartz and granite countertops, tile backsplashes, lighting, and flooring — handled by one licensed residential contractor instead of five phone numbers.

WHAT IT COSTS
Kitchen Remodel Pricing

Kitchens vary more than any other room, so here are honest starting points for the three kinds of kitchen projects we do most.

Small Kitchen Remodel
STARTING AT
$28,000
Most projects $28k–$36k

A smaller kitchen with new cabinets, base-level quartz countertops, backsplash and lighting in the existing layout.

Full Kitchen Remodel
STARTING AT
$36,000
Most projects $36k–$50k

New cabinets, quartz countertops, backsplash, flooring and lighting in your existing layout.

Semi-Custom to Custom
STARTING AT
$50,000
Most projects $50k–$85k+

Semi-custom or custom cabinetry, larger kitchens and layout changes. Cabinet grade is the biggest single jump in price.

Cabinets and countertops are included in these ranges. Appliances, light fixtures and faucets are your selections. Typical ranges to help you plan; your written estimate, built after we see your space, is what your project is priced on.

How Long It Takes

Time on site once work starts. Cabinet lead times come first, which is why we order before we demolish.

Small kitchen remodel
3 to 5 weeks
Full kitchen remodel
4 to 6 weeks
Semi-custom to custom
6 to 10 weeks
Small Choices That Move the Number

Each one is worth it for the right kitchen. They just add up, so it helps to know before you say yes.

Under-cabinet lighting
$1,500–$2,200
Each extra recessed light
$200 each
Vented range hood where there’s no vent today
$5,000–$6,000+
Pot filler over the stove
$800
Moving the microwave (new circuit)
$1,000+
Moving the sink
from $800
See every stage of a kitchen remodel, in order →
Why adding a range hood vent costs so much

If your kitchen doesn’t already have a hood vented outside, adding one is a project of its own: ductwork run through the attic and out the roof, a permit, a roofer to flash the roof penetration, a custom hood cover built out around a range hood insert, and the electrical to power it. That combination easily runs $5,000 to $6,000, and more on some homes. The same goes for moving the microwave into a drawer or a new spot: it needs its own new circuit. Neither is a bad choice. They are simply the two items that surprise people most.

What Really Moves a Kitchen Price

Three decisions drive most of the difference between a $28,000 kitchen and a $70,000 one.

Cabinet grade
Stock to semi-custom to custom is the biggest single jump in a kitchen budget.
Countertops
Price climbs through the tiers, then levels off. Past that, it mostly grows with how many slabs the room needs.
Venting, wiring & plumbing moves
A new hood vent, a relocated microwave circuit or moving the sink adds real cost fast.

How to Compare Two Kitchen Quotes

A cheaper kitchen quote usually means cheaper cabinets or a lower grade of quartz. Before you compare totals, make sure you’re comparing the same things:

All-plywood cabinet boxes, not particleboard
Dovetail drawer boxes
Soft-close hinges
Soft-close, full-extension drawer slides
The quartz brand and grade (lower grades can discolor)
Quartz used indoors only: it’s made for air-conditioned spaces, and direct sun can yellow it
The same countertop tier and edge profile
Permits included where the work requires them

If one quote leaves any of these out, ask. The difference in price is usually the difference in what you’re getting.

OUR APPROACH
One Contractor. One Vision. Zero Coordination Headaches.

A whole-home remodel is the most complex project a homeowner can undertake. We make it simple by handling everything — design, permits, demolition, construction, plumbing, electrical, flooring, painting, and final polish — under one contract, with one project manager who you can call any time.

The Belleair Beach whole-home renovation is our flagship project: exterior, kitchen, living areas, primary suite, bathrooms, flooring, and a custom outdoor shower — all completed by Bayshore Remodels.

WHAT IT COSTS
Whole Home Remodel Pricing

A whole-home project is a collection of decisions. Here is what the most common pieces cost, so you can see how a full remodel adds up.

Kitchen, baths, floors & finishes

Pricing for the Pieces

Most whole-home projects are built from these. The numbers are fairly steady from house to house.

LVP flooring, installed with material
$7–$9 per sq ft
Tile flooring, installed with material
$17–$22 per sq ft

most homes $7,000–$12,000
The one flooring surprise: uneven floors

Flooring prices are pretty predictable. The one thing that can add cost is what we find after the old floor comes up. If large areas of the slab are uneven, they have to be self-leveled before new LVP or tile goes down, or the new floor will flex, click and crack. We price it after demolition, once we can actually see it, and only when it’s needed.

Kitchen pricing →    Bathroom pricing →    Painting →
Why Permitted Work Costs More

When a kitchen or bathroom is permitted, it has to meet today’s code, not the code the house was built to. In a kitchen that usually means new dedicated circuits for the dishwasher, disposal, microwave and refrigerator. In a bathroom it means protected circuits near water, a vent fan that exhausts outside, and plumbing and shower waterproofing that pass inspection. In both, most municipalities now require arc-fault protection on new circuits, which can lead to more rewiring in older homes. It’s a real cost in every permitted room, and it’s the right way to do it.

We walk every room with you and sort what matters most from what can wait.
Plan the order
Kitchen and bathrooms first, then floors, then baseboard and doors, with paint last so nothing gets touched up twice.
Build

Final walkthrough
Room by room, punch list closed out, final clean.

How to Compare Two Whole-Home Quotes

On a project this size, what’s left out matters more than the total. Ask every contractor:

Are permits included where the work requires them?
Is each trade licensed where it needs to be?
Who sets the order of the work and keeps the schedule?
Which materials are included, and which are allowances?
Are demolition, haul-off and cleanup included?
How are surprises found behind walls or under floors handled?

The cheapest whole-home quote is often the one that leaves the most for later.

OUR APPROACH
Professional Cabinet Refinishing — Shop-Quality Finish, In Your Home.

We remove every door and drawer and transport them to our dedicated spray shop, where they receive a premium water-based commercial-grade coating — the same finish used on factory-built cabinetry. While your doors are at the shop, we prep your kitchen: seal it off with dust barriers, fill all nail holes, sand surfaces smooth, and run air scrubbers.

Doors and drawers removed and professionally sprayed at our dedicated shop
Premium water-based commercial-grade coating — durable and eco-conscious
Kitchen sealed and air scrubbers running throughout
Nail holes filled and surfaces sanded before coating
Custom touch-up bottle provided for long-term maintenance
Licensed Residential Contractor CRC1335471 · Fully Insured
WHAT IT COSTS
Cabinet Refinishing Pricing

Refinishing is for when you love your kitchen’s layout and just want a new color and a fresh look, without a full remodel. We price by the piece, so the size of your kitchen drives the number.

Smaller Kitchen
STARTING AT
$5,000
15–20 doors

Every door, drawer and cabinet box sprayed in a factory-style finish.

Medium Kitchen
MOST PROJECTS
$8k–$10k
30 doors, 15 drawers

The most common kitchen we refinish, island panel and hood included.

Large Kitchen
MOST PROJECTS
$11k–$15k
40+ doors

Bigger layouts, more glass doors and panels.

Typical ranges from our recent projects, including typical materials, to help you plan. Your written estimate, built after we see your space, is what your project is priced on.

How Long It Takes

Refinishing and refacing are for when you want your kitchen updated without living through a full remodel. Average time on site:

Cabinet refinishing
5–7 working days
Cabinet refacing
5–7 working days
Refinishing or refacing plus new countertops & backsplash
2–3 weeks
Small Choices That Move the Number
Second color (two-tone)
$500
Soft-close hinges
$10 per hinge
Trash pull-out
$375
Glass doors
cost more per door
Why glass doors cost more

Glass has to be protected or removed and reset, and it can crack in handling. If it does, we replace it, and that risk is built into the price so it never shows up as a surprise. The inside of the cabinet shows through, so we finish it to match.

How It Goes
Consultation
We check the boxes, hinges and under the sink, and tell you honestly if your cabinets are good candidates.
Countertops first
If you’re changing them, the new countertops go in before any cabinet work. Plan on $225 to reconnect the dishwasher.
Spray and finish
Doors are sprayed in our shop; boxes are prepped and sprayed on site.
Back together
Hinges adjusted, hardware installed, walkthrough and a touch-up bottle in your color.
Refinish, Reface or Remodel?
	REFINISHING	REFACING	FULL KITCHEN REMODEL
What changes	Color and finish	Door and drawer style, plus finish	Everything, including the layout
Countertops	Optional. Keep yours or replace them	Optional, unless we add a cabinet or two	Always replaced, and included in our ranges
Starting price	From $5,000	From $7,000	From $28,000
Time on site	5 to 7 working days	5 to 7 working days	3 to 10 weeks
Best when	Boxes and doors are solid and you like the style	Boxes are solid but you want a new door style	The layout or the cabinet boxes no longer work
Our Warranty, in Writing
2 years
Against blistering and peeling on your sprayed finish.
1 year
Written workmanship warranty on every project.
Manufacturer
Many of the products we use carry their own material warranties. Because we are licensed professionals installing to the manufacturer’s specifications, those warranties carry through to your project.

Full terms and exclusions are in your signed agreement.

Questions to Ask Any Refinisher

Refinishing quotes vary because the prep varies. Before you compare prices, ask:

Are the doors sprayed in a shop, or brushed and rolled in place?
How are the cabinets degreased and sanded before priming?
What primer and topcoat are used, and how durable is the finish?
How is the rest of the kitchen protected while the boxes are sprayed?
Are hinges adjusted and new hardware installed?
Do I get touch-up paint in my exact color?

A finish only lasts as long as the prep under it.

Built by Specialists, Not a Jack-of-All-Trades

Every part of the job is done by someone who only does that work, coordinated by one project manager.

Here is exactly what to expect, step by step.

We reach out within one business day

Our office calls or texts you back to set up a time to talk.

A quick call

What you want to change, your timeline and a ballpark budget. If we’re not the right fit, we’ll tell you then and point you to someone who is.

Free consultation at your home

About 30 minutes. We look at the space, measure, check what’s behind the work (plumbing, electrical, condition) and talk through options.

Your written estimate

The work broken out by trade, what’s included, what’s a selection, and a timeline. Usually within a day for smaller jobs, a few days for design projects. No obligation.

You decide

No pressure and no pushy follow-ups. If you move forward, we plan selections and order materials before anything is torn out.

Together.

1-year written workmanship warranty. Paint carries a 2-year warranty against blistering and peeling, and products carry the manufacturer warranty.
Deposit, then progress payments. A deposit gets you on the schedule; the rest is paid in draws as the work progresses, so you never pay far ahead of the work.
One project manager. One person to call from planning through the final walkthrough.

HOW WE WORK
No Sales Pitch.
Just How It Actually Goes.

Who we’re a good fit for, who we’re not, how a project runs from the first call to the final walkthrough, and the terms we hold ourselves to. If something here doesn’t sit right with you, better you know now.

Are We the Right Fit?

We’d rather tell you up front than waste your time, or ours.

We’re a great fit if…
Your project involves three or more trades, like plumbing, electrical, tile and cabinets. That’s where a general contractor earns their keep.
You want it done right and permitted, not just done cheap.
You’re planning a kitchen from $28,000, a bathroom from $15,500, cabinets from $5,000 or a whole home from $150,000.
You live in Pinellas, Hillsborough or Pasco. We take on select Sarasota and Lakewood Ranch projects when the job makes sense.
You want one person to call, a written scope and no surprises.
We’re probably not the right fit if…
You only need one trade, like an interior paint job or new soffits. You can hire that trade directly, and we’re happy to refer the subs we trust.
You’re looking for the lowest number no matter what’s behind it.
You’d rather manage the trades and judge the work yourself. That’s a fair choice, and some homeowners do it well.

Not sure whether you need a contractor at all? Ask us. We’ll tell you honestly.

“Everybody is specialized and they only do what they do. There’s no guy jack-of-all-trading in there.”
JUSTIN, OWNER

Every stage of your project is done by someone who only does that trade, with at least 10 years in it, coordinated by one project manager. Specialists move faster and cleaner through their stage, and that’s a big part of how we keep a schedule.

If You’ve Been Burned by a Contractor Before

We hear it all the time: paid a lot up front and the job dragged on, the contractor disappeared, the price kept climbing, nobody called back. Here’s how we’re set up differently.

How we’re set up
A deposit, then progress payments. You pay as the work gets done, never far ahead of it.
Materials before demolition. Cabinets, tile and fixtures are ordered and on the way before anything comes out, so your kitchen never sits gutted.
One project manager. One person to call from planning through the walkthrough.
A written scope, broken out by trade. You know exactly what you’re paying for.
When something comes up
Things come up on every remodel. Rot behind a dishwasher, two layers of old flooring, wiring that isn’t to code.
When we find something, we stop, show you, and price it in writing before any extra work happens.
What keeps a timeline isn’t luck. It’s preparing properly and walking down that road before work starts: selections made, materials on site, trades sequenced, inspections planned in.
Why We Ask About Your Budget

It isn’t so we can spend all of it. Knowing your number tells us what’s realistic, so we can build a package that fits: the right scope, the right materials and the right finish level for what you want to spend. If what you want and what you want to spend don’t line up, we’ll tell you before you’ve paid for anything. See what projects cost.

How a Project Goes

From the first call to the final walkthrough.

A quick call

We reach out within one business day. What you want to change, your timeline and a ballpark budget.

Free 30-minute consultation

At your home. We look at the space, measure and check what’s behind the work.

Your written estimate

Broken out by trade. Usually within a day for smaller jobs, a few days for design projects.

Design & selections

A 3D rendering on every kitchen, and on bathrooms when you want one. Every selection made before we start.

Order, then build

Materials ordered and confirmed first. Then each specialist does their stage, in order.

Walkthrough & warranty

We walk it with you, close out every punch-list item, and put the warranty in writing.

Our Terms in Plain English

The short version of what you can hold us to.

Consultations are free. So is the written estimate.
Your estimate is the price. It holds for 30 days.
Changes are approved in writing first. Always.
Permits when required. Permitted work meets today’s code, which costs more and protects you when you sell.
Your own materials are welcome. They need to be on site before the trades need them.
1-year written workmanship warranty. Products carry the manufacturer warranty.
Paint: 2 years against blistering and peeling, plus a 30-day touch-up visit.
Licensed and insured. Florida residential contractor CRC1335471.
Family Owned. Faith First. Giving Back.

A few things about who we are that don’t fit on an estimate.

Family owned and operated

When you call, you’re talking to the family that owns the company, not a call center or a franchise. Your project matters to us because our name is on it.

Faith first

Our faith shapes how we run this business: tell people the truth, price fairly, keep our word, and treat your home the way we’d want ours treated.

Giving back to animal rescues

Animal rescues are close to our hearts. We support Rescue Dogs Dream, an all-volunteer dog rescue from Justin’s hometown that takes in at-risk, senior and sick shelter dogs and cares for them until they find a home.

Refinish, Reface or Remodel?
How to Choose for Your Kitchen.

Three questions decide it. Here’s how we walk Tampa Bay homeowners through the choice, with real prices, timelines and what each option can’t do.

Find Your Answer
Ask Us to Look
The short answer

If your cabinet boxes are solid and you like your layout, you don’t need a remodel. Keep your door style and change the color with refinishing, from $5,000. Change the door style with refacing, from $7,000. If the layout doesn’t work or the boxes are failing, a kitchen remodel, from $28,000, is the better spend.

THREE QUESTIONS
Answer These in Order
1. Are your cabinet boxes solid?

Look under the sink for water damage, check for sagging shelves, and see whether doors still hang straight.

If the boxes are damaged or failing, refinishing and refacing won’t fix that. You’re looking at a kitchen remodel.

2. Do you like your layout?

If you want to move cabinets, open a wall or add an island, that’s a kitchen remodel.

If you only want to add a cabinet or two, refacing can do it, with new countertops as part of the project.

3. Do you like your door style?

Yes: refinishing. Your doors are sprayed in our shop with a new color and a factory-style finish.

No, or the doors are thermofoil or peeling laminate: refacing. New doors and drawer fronts on the boxes you already have, with soft-close hinges and drawer slides standard.

SIDE BY SIDE
How the Three Options Compare
	REFINISHING	REFACING	FULL KITCHEN REMODEL
What changes	Color and finish	Door and drawer style, plus finish	Everything, including the layout
Countertops	Optional. Keep yours or replace them	Optional, unless we add a cabinet or two	Always replaced, and included in our ranges
Starting price	From $5,000	From $7,000	From $28,000
Most medium kitchens	$8,000–$10,000	$10,000–$12,500	$36,000–$50,000
Time on site	5 to 7 working days	5 to 7 working days	3 to 10 weeks
Warranty	2-year finish, 1-year workmanship	2-year finish, 1-year workmanship	1-year workmanship
Best when	Boxes and doors are solid and you like the style	Boxes are solid but you want a new door style	The layout or the cabinet boxes no longer work

Typical ranges from our recent projects, to help you plan. Your written estimate, built after we see your space, is what your project is priced on.

The countertop rule

With refinishing and refacing, keeping your countertops is your choice. Add a cabinet or two during refacing and new countertops become part of the project. With a full remodel, new countertops are always included. Whenever countertops change, they go in before any cabinet work.

HONEST LIMITS
What Each Option Can’t Do
Refinishing
It won’t change your door style or fix damaged boxes.
The finish lasts when the prep is right. Poor prep is why refinished cabinets peel, so we degrease, sand and prime every surface, and warranty against blistering and peeling for two years.
Refacing
It depends on sound cabinet boxes. Water-damaged or failing boxes aren’t good candidates.
It can add a cabinet or two, not move them. A new layout is a remodel.
Kitchen remodel
It takes the longest: 3 to 10 weeks on site, after cabinet lead times.
Walls and floors can hide damage you only find at demolition. We order materials first so your kitchen isn’t torn out while you wait.
